pages.name: Cut every piece in two
pages.text: This bar shows 3/4. Cut every piece in two and it shows 6/8. The shaded amount hasn't changed, so 3/4 and 6/8 are [[equivalent]].

pages.name: Cut a quarter in two
pages.task: This bar shows 1/4. Cut each piece in two, then pick its new name.
pages.why: Cutting each piece in two makes 8 pieces, and the shaded quarter becomes 2 of them. The amount stays the same.

pages.name: Times 3, top and bottom
pages.text: Cut each third into 3 and there are 3 times as many pieces, and 3 times as many shaded. So 2/3 becomes 6/9. The top and the bottom are both multiplied by 3.

pages.name: Fill in the gap
pages.why: The bottom went from 4 to 8, so every quarter was cut in two. Each shaded quarter became two eighths, so the top doubles too.

pages.name: The same amount
pages.task: This bar shows 3/5. Which of these is the same amount?
pages.why: Multiply the top and the bottom by 2. Each fifth becomes two tenths, so three fifths become six tenths.

pages.name: Join pieces back
pages.text: Now go back the other way. Join the pieces in pairs and 6/8 becomes 3/4. Joining divides the top and the bottom by the same number. Joining as far as it will go is called [[simplifying]].

pages.name: Simplify 4/8
pages.task: Simplify 4/8 as far as it goes.
pages.why: Divide the top and the bottom by 4. Four eighths join into one half, and a single shaded piece has no shaded partner to join, so 1/2 is as simple as it gets.

pages.name: Simplify 6/9
pages.why: Divide the top and the bottom by 3. Each group of three ninths joins into one third.

pages.name: One place on the line
pages.text: The bars for 1/2, 2/4 and 4/8 shade the same amount. Drop down to the line and all three land on one mark. Equivalent fractions sit at the same place on the line.

pages.alt: Three bars of the same length, cut into halves, quarters and eighths, with 3 of them shaded to 1/2, 2/4 and 4/8, above a number line from 0 to 1. One line drops from the end of all three shadings to a single mark, labelled 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8.

pages.name: Find 6/8 on the line
pages.task: Tap where 6/8 goes on the line.
pages.why: Six eighth-steps from 0 land on the same mark as three quarter-steps. So 6/8 and 3/4 are the same number.

pages.name: A drill bit in sixteenths
pages.task: A drill bit is 3/8 inch. How many sixteenths is that?
pages.why: An eighth is two sixteenths, so multiply the top and the bottom by 2. A 3/8 inch bit is 6/16 inch.

pages.name: Not a half
pages.task: Which of these is not equal to 1/2?
pages.why: 3/6 and 5/10 both simplify to 1/2. Two thirds is more than a half.
